messages:
Olivia: Acme support just opened an escalation. Their latency dashboard in Console lost the p95/p99 lines after today's capacity rollout in prod-us-west. P50/P90 and averages still show, tails are gone. They included screenshots and a 72h window they were looking at.

Maya: Can you drop the dashboard link and exact time range the customer used?

Olivia: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/latency?env=prod-us-west&range=72h
Timeframe: last 72h, issue starts around 2026-03-17T12:05Z right after the rollout.

deploy-bot: deployment event  capacity-rollout/v2 promoted to prod-us-west at 2026-03-17T12:04:40Z (rev: cr-507)

Alex (sre): Looping in eng-sre. @eng-sre-oncall any quick thoughts? Could be a metric rename or transform.

eng-sre-oncall: Investigating. I queried TSDB directly for the percentile series and see data for p95/p99 for service=acme-proxy. But the dashboard panels render no quantile curves.

Jun: What was the raw query you ran?

eng-sre-oncall: PromQL I used against metrics-cache:
```
max_over_time(latency_quantile{service=\"acme-proxy\",quantile=\"0.95\"}[72h])
```
It returns series with non-empty samples.

Rami: We shipped an ingest-transform tweak in the capacity rollout that changes histogram-to-quantile exports. The metric names now include punctuation: e.g. latency.quantile_0.95 instead of the old latency_p95.

Maya: If the panel is filtering by legacy name patterns the new dotted names would be excluded. Can someone check the panel's series regex/alias?

Alex (sre): Confirmed. The Grafana panel had a regex expecting names without dots (legacy: latency_p95). The ingest change emits names with dots, so the filter matches nothing and the curves vanish.

Olivia: Customer is anxious. Any short-term workaround we can give them while we fix infra?

eng-sre-oncall: Short term: run the raw PromQL in Explore or update the panel query to match the new metric names. Example to share with Acme:
```
max_over_time(latency_quantile{service=\"acme-proxy\",quantile=\"0.95\"}[1h])
max_over_time(latency_quantile{service=\"acme-proxy\",quantile=\"0.99\"}[1h])
```
I sent that snippet to their support contact.

Jun: For a durable fix we have two paths: (1) rollback the ingest-transform rename from the rollout (fast, global fix), or (2) add aliasing/mapping so both old and new metric name styles are emitted and update dashboards to be name-agnostic. Ops preference?

Alex (sre): Start with rollback to restore customers quickly. Then plan a schema migration with aliases to avoid breaking dashboards on future rollouts.

Maya: I opened ticket RDW-2345: "ingest-transform: revert metric name change for percentile exports; add alias mapping" and assigned to eng-ml. Notified Acme with the Explore query and that we're rolling back.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for capacity-rollout/v2 in prod-us-west at 2026-03-17T12:52:10Z (executor: platform-oncall)

eng-sre-oncall: After rollback I can see p95/p99 series render on the dashboard again for Acme's workspace. Requested a confirmation screenshot from the customer.

Olivia: Customer confirmed lines returned and they're unblocked. They asked for a postmortem and assurance this won't happen again.

Alex (sre): We'll own the postmortem and the migration plan. Adding Jun and me to RDW-2345. We'll include steps for aliasing and a test checklist for future ingest changes.

Maya: I'll update the support ticket and follow up with customer comms. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
